item.title: Artemis 1.2.0
item.description:
The 1.2 beta. A browsing agent, sites as apps, uBlock Origin Lite out of the box, and the speed push from the last few nightlies. It's everything since 1.1.0, so it's a big one.

New

  • A browsing agent that runs on your own Claude Code. Open it beside the page with ⌃⌘A, keep your chats, and pick Manual, Auto or Bypass for what it may do without asking. It's off until you turn it on in Settings › Intelligence
  • Install a site as an app: Install as App… in the page's More menu or the File menu gives it its own glass window, Dock icon and ⌘-Tab entry. Click its name at the top to change its icon, frame colour and toolbar, keep it on top, or show a Dock badge for unread counts. They live in Settings › Links › Apps (report)
  • Turn trackers, ads and cookie banners on or off per site, from the site's settings. Settings › Privacy & Security lists every site you've changed
  • uBlock Origin Lite comes installed and on, unless you already run another full blocker. Remove it and it stays gone
  • Links to other sites from a favourite or pinned tab open in Peek, so the tab stays where you left it. A click on a favourite never reloads it, and a double-click takes it home (report)
  • Updates download and install inside Artemis, with a glowing bar in Settings and the sidebar in the colour of the update's channel, and a switch to install them automatically
  • What's New: the first time an update opens, a short moment shows what it brought, in that update's own colour
  • Filter downloads in the Library by kind and type, and sort them. The filter panel closes from the same spot that opens it
  • Extensions from the Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons keep themselves up to date, and so do blocklists
  • Open new tabs as a page instead of the command bar, with your extension's new tab page if it has one (Settings › Tabs › New Tabs) (report)
  • The command bar finishes sites you visit often as you type, so a few letters and ↵ gets you there (report)
  • Gift Artemis to a Friend, from the Library, the app menu or the command bar
  • An About pane with the changelog, log export and a hard reset, and a Media pane for the mini-player and Now Playing
  • Trust a site to open one app, or any app, per profile
  • ⌘Z steps back through the theme editor while it's open

Refined

  • Opens a window in 481 ms
  • 1.9 GB with 48 tabs open
  • New tabs paint in 62 ms, and the first one after launch no longer flashes blank
  • The sidebar slides with about a third less work

*Medians on one Mac with M1 Pro, measured 24 November 2026. Memory counts every process Artemis runs, and the 48 tabs are real web pages.*

  • The Library slides over the page instead of pushing it, so the page never jumps, and its panel widens smoothly as it opens (report)
  • Peek opens on a firm press, straight away, with no dimming zoom, and names the site it shows above the page (report)
  • Closing a tab goes back to the tab you were on before (again)
  • A link from another app brings up only its Scout window, and the main window stays where it was
  • Every AI feature is off by default, each with its own switch and a note on where it runs
  • Favourites never show the away slash, so the row stays clean wherever you've browsed
  • Four favourites share a row at the default sidebar width (report)
  • The traffic lights live in the sidebar and behave the same everywhere
  • The sidebar's scroller is wider, and a scroll anywhere beside the tab list scrolls the list, not the page
  • Blocking is three plain switches and a pop-up ads list, and onboarding asks about cookie banners and clutter
  • Imported bookmarks land in one folder in your first space, and importing again doesn't duplicate them. On a fresh install, imported spaces replace the empty starter one
  • Tabs sleep sooner, a woken tab keeps its last look until it has loaded, and tabs with unsent text or a running download stay awake
  • The mini-player only resizes when your fingers spread, not on a swipe or click-drag (report)
  • Settings are regrouped: tab sleep is in Tabs, folders in Sidebar, the data folder in About
  • Boosts are retired. Their data is kept but no longer applied

Fixed

  • YouTube and other pages that redirect to another site no longer hang (report)
  • Gmail and other sites that move as they load stay on their favourite's or pinned tab's home page, so a pinned tab only shows the away slash once you've really left (report)
  • ⌘-Tab back to Artemis keeps you on the Space with its window, fullscreen included
  • Switching spaces, the background colour now moves in step with the slide
  • fn⌃F Fill and fn⌃C Center tile the window again (report)
  • Swiping back and forward lands where you left the page, and settles cleanly (report)
  • Pages typed into ⌘T start loading sooner
  • A fresh ⌘T bar keeps every key you type, ↵ right after a paste opens what you pasted, and the hint no longer sticks on "⌘↵ Open in Split"
  • Suggested strong passwords always rate as strong
  • Pages opened in the background load their images at the right size
  • A page you close falls silent at once (report)
  • Menu shortcuts work straight after something changes, and the tab shortcuts follow your keyboard layout and stay out of the Web Inspector's way
  • A closed window no longer brings its new-tab bar back with the next one
  • A tab opened by AppleScript with an address no longer opens the command bar
  • If saving your tabs fails, for example on a full disk, Artemis tries again and tells you in the sidebar
  • Fingerprint Defence leaves small and see-through canvas images exact, so sites that draw them look right
  • User script managers install and run scripts properly, and more Chrome extension features work: 29 of the 50 most popular extensions now work fully, including Adobe Acrobat, MetaMask, Zotero and Volume Master
  • uBlock Origin Lite's pop-up fills its panel, and its element zapper and picker work
  • An extension removed while it updates stays removed, and a tab opened from an extension's page can reach sites again
  • Coding agents connected to Artemis ask once per install, and say why a call can't run
  • Restoring a backup tells you what it will merge and names any scripts it carries
  • Crash reports no longer fire when a page's process ends normally
  • Saved .webarchive pages open without freezing Artemis
  • Password recipes only fill on secure pages, and say when a site's name looks like one you've saved
  • Site permissions like camera and location, and certificates you chose to trust, are kept per profile. Incognito ones are forgotten when its windows close, and exporting passwords always asks for your password again
  • The address bar always shows the end of a long site name, where the real site is, and site permission and login prompts only appear over the tab that asked
  • Security fixes for extensions, user scripts, downloads, passwords, passkeys, locked spaces and links that open other apps

item.title: Artemis 1.1.0
item.description:
Everything from the 1.1 beta and the nightlies since, in one update: bring your old browser with you, and a long list of fixes.

New

  • Import from Arc, Chrome, Firefox, Safari and almost any browser like them. Spaces, profiles, pinned tabs, folders, splits, bookmarks, history and logins come over, and each profile of the old browser becomes its own
  • Onboarding on first launch (replay it from Settings › General)
  • Settings search finds single settings, not just pages, and takes you straight to them
  • Put the sidebar on the right, in Settings › Appearance › Sidebar
  • Hold ⌃⇥ to pick a recent tab from cards
  • Drag the space icons at the bottom of the sidebar to reorder your spaces (report)
  • Space theme edits show live as you make them; the tick saves, the x puts it back. Glass spaces get a brightness slider (report)
  • Throw the mini-player off a screen edge to tuck it away; a glass notch stays to tap, pull or slide along the edge (report)
  • Drag downloaded files out of the Library and the downloads peek (report)
  • Sites that need Chrome get Chrome's headers and browser features, not just its user agent
  • Reader finds articles with Mozilla Readability
  • Install a Safari extension from its app, in Extensions › From Disk
  • New spaces suggest icons from their name, and icon search knows what words mean, so "home" finds a house
  • A Nightly update channel in Settings › General › Updates, and Nebula, a new app icon colour

Refined

  • The Library's buttons are bigger, and the Library keeps one width however wide the sidebar is (report)
  • A new password's suggestions lead with the strong random one, then your recipes; new recipes use a site's first three letters
  • Overshooting the window's edge still reveals the hidden sidebar, and passing over it on the way in doesn't (report)
  • The recent downloads peek opens faster, waits a second first, and is rounded like the buttons under it
  • Fullscreen keeps working traffic lights in the sidebar
  • Filter lists convert with AdGuard's SafariConverterLib, so more of their rules work

Fixed

  • Proton Pass: the popup opens at full size, and the Firefox build can finish signing in (report)
  • Google lets you create a passkey in Artemis, and saved passkeys are offered under sign-in fields (report)
  • The PDF viewer's download button saves the file, and downloads from new-tab links go ahead (report)
  • Check for Updates offers an update that's already waiting (report)
  • A picked icon stays in the Dock after quitting (report)
  • Jumping to a space two or more away, by ⌃⇥ or any other way, no longer leaves the sidebar showing the space in between
  • ⌃⇥ works when the keyboard is in a page
  • Delete no longer goes back a page, so sites that use the key keep it
  • Closing a window no longer crashes
  • ⇧⌘V pastes and matches style, even right after a new tab or an undo (report)
  • A link from another app opens Scout alone, in front; a Dock click after closing the last window opens one window, not two (report)
  • No second browser window at launch (report)
  • Incognito and new windows open even with no browser window open
  • Hiding the sidebar from the keyboard or a menu slides it away at once, with no freeze first
  • The hovered link's address moves out of the pointer's way, and goes when its page does
  • The glass around a selected tab or the address field is no longer cut off at its sides
  • Pages an extension sends a tab to, like uBlock's blocked-site warning and its Proceed, load as normal tabs
  • Extensions see Peek pages as tabs; reloading a turned-off extension's page returns to the site (report, report)
  • Connecting a VPN extension no longer brings up a macOS proxy password prompt
  • Uploads that only take images, like Bluesky's avatar picker, no longer grey out every file
  • Reader shows the whole article on sites that fold their sections, keeps only http, https and mailto links, and runs no script
  • A site's camera, microphone or location prompt can't be answered by a key or a click already on its way; Remember starts unticked
  • An extension archive that won't unpack is refused instead of loaded unchecked
  • Filter lists past WebKit's rule limit keep every exception

item.title: Artemis 1.1.0
item.description:
Bring everything over from the browser you're leaving, and get shown around on your first launch.

New

  • Import from Arc, Chrome, Firefox, Safari and almost any browser like them. Spaces, profiles, pinned tabs, folders, splits, bookmarks, history and logins come over, and each profile of the old browser becomes its own.
  • Onboarding has been added, and I think it's pretty gorgeous!! Tell me what you think (Replay it from Settings › General).
  • Settings search finds single settings, not just pages, and takes you straight to them. Describe what you want and it finds the setting.
  • New spaces suggest icons from their name, and icon search knows what words mean, so "home" finds a house.
  • An empty space shows the Artemis mark. Drag it to spin it.
  • A Nightly update channel in Settings › General › Updates, for the newest builds.
  • Nebula, a new app icon colour.

Fixed

  • Pages an extension sends a tab to, like uBlock's blocked-site warning, load instead of showing an error.
  • Connecting a VPN extension no longer brings up a macOS proxy password prompt.
  • Uploads that only take images, like Bluesky's avatar picker, no longer grey out every file.
  • A link opened from another app brings Scout to the front.

item.title: Artemis 1.0.0
item.description:
Artemis 1.0 is here, and it's open source under the GPL 3.0. Every part of the browser was gone through for this release, and more than 300 problems were fixed.

It needs macOS 26 or later on an M1 or newer Mac.

New

  • Built for liquid glass. Choose Glass in a space's theme, then set how frosted the sidebar and the window behind it are, all the way to clear.
  • Live folders fill themselves from a GitHub repo or a feed.
  • Hover over a pinned tab or a favourite to preview it. Mail tabs show what's new in your inbox.
  • ⌘Z undoes changes in the sidebar and in Settings.
  • Each space remembers which favourite it was showing.
  • Ask the page summarises the page, and offers what it knows when the page doesn't say.
  • A tab keeps a name you give it.
  • A count in a tab's title, like (12), shows as a badge.
  • Hold a dragged tab near the top or bottom of the sidebar and the list scrolls. The closer to the edge, the faster.

Refined

Privacy and security

  • Extensions only get what their permissions allow. Reading a site with your cookies, changing the proxy or reading the clipboard each need the permission the extension asked for.
  • Incognito leaves less behind. Certificates you accept, where downloads came from, and sites played in the mini-player are no longer saved.
  • A locked space asks for Touch ID as soon as you arrive on it, and keeps its pages out of menus and off the disk. Turning off its lock, deleting it or undoing a move out of it needs Touch ID.
  • A page asks before it starts a download.
  • Copied passwords and codes are hidden from clipboard managers and don't stay on the clipboard.
  • Clearing history also clears recently closed tabs, back and forward lists, and site icons from that time.
  • Search suggestions and site icons go through your profile's VPN extension, as pages do.

Windows and tabs

  • With several windows open, closing one no longer breaks sign-in popups, camera and microphone requests, or history in the tabs it opened.
  • With every window closed, ⌘T, History and the other commands open a new window.
  • ⇧⌘T brings back a group of closed tabs together, in order.
  • The sidebar's scroll bar is thinner and sits in the margin, clear of your tabs.
  • Delete Space asks first. So does removing an extension.

Mini-player

  • Pinch to resize it, even while another app is in front.
  • It sits flush against the side of the screen and moves between displays smoothly.

Your data

  • Passwords stay intact if Artemis is interrupted while saving them.
  • A session file that can't be read is set aside, never written over.
  • Restoring a backup keeps the profiles already on this Mac.

Quicker

  • History search keeps up with your typing, even with a large history.
  • Content blocking is ready sooner after a relaunch.
  • Installing an extension, exporting passwords and importing from another browser no longer pause the browser.

Fixed

  • Clicks on the floating sidebar no longer reach the page under it.
  • ⌘W in an incognito window closes the tab, not the window.
  • A page you trusted past a certificate warning never shows as Secure.
  • Local pages load their own stylesheets, images and linked pages.
  • The Now Playing bar and a tab's speaker show only while something plays.
  • Many smaller fixes across the sidebar, split view, the mini-player, the command bar, password autofill and VoiceOver.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.7
item.description:
It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

New in 0.9.7

  • Addresses and cards. Artemis fills your saved addresses and cards from a list under the field, and offers to save new ones when you submit a form. Each profile keeps its own. Card numbers stay in your keychain and security codes are never saved.
  • You choose when to unlock. Passwords, cards and addresses each have their own setting: every time, after a few minutes, until you quit, or never. Locking your Mac or letting it sleep locks them all again.
  • Import from your other browsers. Bookmarks and history, into the profile you pick. It's in Settings › General.
  • Shortcuts and Siri. Open pages, switch spaces, find tabs, or grab the current page as Markdown. Showing your spaces and tabs in Spotlight is off until you turn it on in Settings › Privacy.
  • Unread badges. Sites can show a count on their pinned tab or favourite.
  • Translation keeps up as a page changes, reaches into frames, and can translate a site every time. Long pages no longer freeze while they translate.
  • VoiceOver names every control around the page and gives sidebar rows their actions.
  • Reduce Motion turns slides and zooms into fades.

Better

  • Switching tabs, crossfades and dragging split dividers are smoother.
  • Picture in Picture always uses Artemis's own mini-player.
  • A page that keeps crashing now says so, with a Reload button, instead of reloading over and over.

Fixed

  • Routing rules, addresses and cards changed just before quitting could be lost.
  • A backup that couldn't be saved or read failed without saying so.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.6
item.description:
It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

New in 0.9.6

  • Extensions in incognito. Each extension now has an Allow in incognito switch in Settings › Extensions, off by default. Extensions that ask never to run in incognito won't, and an extension you allow there can't write your incognito pages into history.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.5
item.description:
A fix release. It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

Fixed in 0.9.5

  • Artemis could crash on launch when there was no page to restore, for example on a fresh install. Fixed.

New

  • AppleScript and Shortcuts can list and control Artemis's windows, spaces and tabs. Running JavaScript inside pages from a script stays off unless you turn it on in Settings › Privacy.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.4
item.description:
A quick follow-up to 0.9.3. It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

Fixed in 0.9.4

  • The download animation now actually shows: the file flies from where you clicked into the Library button.
  • With the sidebar hidden, downloads appear in a small pill at the window's bottom-left, and the file flies there instead.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.3
item.description:
The fourth alpha of Artemis for macOS. It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

New in 0.9.3

  • Downloads you can see. A new download flies from where you clicked into the Library button, a ring around it fills as it arrives, and a pill above the sidebar footer shows the file, its progress and a tick when it's done. Click it to open the file (⌘-click shows it in Finder). The Dock icon counts running downloads.
  • Check for Updates is in the command bar (⌘T, type "update"), as well as the Artemis menu.
  • The address bar stays put properly when the sidebar opens or closes under it.

If you're on 0.9.2, this arrives on its own: look for Relaunch to Update at the bottom of the sidebar.

item.title: Artemis 0.9.2
item.description:
The third alpha of Artemis for macOS. It needs macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon.

New in 0.9.2

  • Automatic updates. From this version on, Artemis updates itself: new versions download quietly, then a Relaunch to Update button appears in the sidebar. Choose Release or Beta in Settings › General › Updates.
  • Send Feedback (Help menu) now posts your message as a public issue here, so you can follow it. Your email, screenshot and page address always stay private, and Keep this private posts nothing public.

If you're on 0.9.1, download this one by hand once; after that, updates arrive on their own.

Opening it the first time: this build isn't notarised by Apple yet, so macOS stops it the first time. Open System Settings › Privacy & Security, click Open Anyway next to Artemis, then click Open. You only do this once.
